analysis:
Examined the docs/developer/test.md head excerpts (lines 2731-3419) and the patch to scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py. The markdown changes are test documentation only: they describe CPU, metadata and hardware test procedures for MiMo, Qwen, Gemma and GLM batching, prefix tenant partitioning, SSD prefix record encoding, cluster service stop ordering and placement. They add no executable behavior. The prefix tenant partition and SSD record sections restate existing T-041 controls (tenant-scoped HMAC lookup, per-tenant records) and do not weaken them. The doc text repeatedly says that synthetic checks do not establish hardware or full-artifact qualification, which matches the threat model's no-overclaim stance (T-056).

The Python file is a CI routing test script. The patch removes `required` from the build-cluster, build-provider and cluster-release-checks lanes, so those lanes now ask the compute plane without a size while DARKBLOOM_JOB_SHAPES is off, rather than staying on Blacksmith. It also updates UNSIZED_PLAN_REQUEST and the cap-order tests, and adds a test that keeps the `required` fallback behavior. This is a test-only change to expectations. The actual routing implementation and workflow files are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that they match. No threat-model asset (A-001 through A-020) or trust boundary is touched by the visible changes. One integration question remains: whether the unseen provider-plan.yml and routing script have the same lane table. That concerns CI runner selection for build jobs, which may include release builds, and is outside the provider runtime threat model. The docs mention that release workflows keep literal runners, so I found no regression.
